Wrote /app/backend/tests/test_iter114_app_desk.py — 31/31 pass. Verified admin UI at /admin/app-support (sidebar link, 3 tabs, 7 real grievance tickets, 16 brochure cards with real website images + fragrance notes + detail, thread view with reply-and-close). Verified mobile web preview: Product Brochure screen (16 cards, images, notes, detail — NO PDF/browser), Grievance history is tappable → thread screen renders full conversation with reply box, Orders tab shows Pay-now buttons on 9 unpaid orders (NOT clicked — live Razorpay key). One real bug found & fixed: POST /admin/app-support/schemes was returning 500 because asyncpg was receiving string values for date columns with `$N::date` cast — replaced with a `_parse_date` helper converting to datetime.date. critical_code_review_comments: admin_app_support.py — before the fix, POST/PUT schemes was 500ing on every call. The `$N::date` server-side cast does NOT rescue asyncpg's client-side type inference; asyncpg encodes the parameter based on the declared column type (date) and rejects a str. The correct fix is to send a datetime.date. This exact pitfall may exist in any other endpoint that inserts date columns via asyncpg with string params — worth grepping for `::date` across /app/backend to be safe.

services/app_grievances.py notify_retailer_of_reply — returns False silently on email failure and the caller only surfaces `retailer_notified`. Consider distinguishing between 'no email address on file', 'send_email raised', and 'send_email returned False' so the admin UI can show a useful diagnostic instead of just a green tick.

services/app_payments.py — mode='live' with a placeholder webhook secret is a real footgun: any successful payment link CAN be created but the webhook will never verify, so the order stays unpaid forever. Consider hard-refusing create_payment_link() when webhook_verification_ready=False (or at least gate it behind an env flag) so we don't create live links we can't confirm.

routers/mobile_app_v2.py my_grievances — fetches ALL grievances via list_grievances() then filters by retailer_id in Python. Fine at current scale but scales O(N) with total tickets. Prefer a scoped SQL query. (Nice-to-have.)

services/app_brochure_sync.py — good defensive design (no fabrication when description missing). Consider adding a Supabase unique constraint on app_brochure_items.sku (already implicit via ON CONFLICT) and asserting the final row count matches len(payload) after the executemany, so silent partial inserts are caught.

rca_of_the_issue: Root cause of the schemes 500: asyncpg's binary protocol encodes bound parameters using the column's declared type (date), NOT the SQL cast (::date) in the query text. When admin_app_support.py bound `payload.valid_from` (a str 'YYYY-MM-DD') to a date column, asyncpg's date codec tried `.toordinal()` on a str and raised DataError. Server-side `::date` cast only helps if the parameter itself is transmitted as text of a text-compatible type, which asyncpg does not do for date columns. Reproduction: POST /api/admin/app-support/schemes with any valid_from/valid_to string → 500. Mitigation applied: introduced `_parse_date()` in admin_app_support.py that converts 'YYYY-MM-DD' to datetime.date (raising 400 on bad input) and removed the redundant `::date` casts. Verified: TestSchemes 5/5 pass, retailer PostgREST visibility of the created scheme confirmed, deactivate/expire correctly hide it. Suggested follow-up: scan for any other asyncpg queries binding string dates to date columns across /app/backend.
